scoring_justification: Absolute effective bond orders and phonon frequencies are strongly method-dependent; the paper's headline claim is the sign of pressure-induced changes (donor/acceptor assignment and blue-shift). Therefore scoring verifies monotonic trends between 0 and 1.0 GPa.

hidden_assets.purpose: expected sign of effective bond order change and phonon blue-shift
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Figure 5 and Figure 3(b); donor/acceptor identification from pressure‑dependent effective bond orders, and blue shift of phonon frequencies.
hidden_assets.generation_method: paper-reported trends: C‑H and N‑O bond orders decrease, N‑N bond orders increase, C‑N bond order nearly constant; all phonon frequencies increase with pressure.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: trends are directly from the paper's quantitative analysis and figures.

outputs.description: Table of effective bond orders for selected C–H, C–N, N–N, and N–O bonds at three hydrostatic pressures. Monotonic trends will be scored.
Table of zone‑centre phonon frequencies at three hydrostatic pressures. The blue‑shift trend will be scored.

output_contract.notes: The scored quantities are monotonic trends, not exact absolute values. The hidden checker compares the sign of changes (slope) against the paper's reported trends.

steps.description: Verify that C‑H and N‑O effective bond orders decrease from 0 to 1.0 GPa, N‑N bond orders increase, and C‑N remains nearly constant.
Verify that every zone‑centre phonon frequency at 1.0 GPa is greater than at 0 GPa (blue shift).
